nodes.description: The cervical lymph nodes are the commonest metastatic site, involved in 10 to 33 per cent of patients. The incidence at diagnosis is 5 to 8 per cent and rises to 20 to 25 per cent later, so neck involvement is more often a development during follow-up than a presenting feature. It is also what the modified Kadish system calls stage D, the stage with by far the worst reported survival.

nodes.description: Single-cell transcriptomics of tumour parenchyma found a conserved globose basal cell regulatory circuit governing divergent neuronal versus sustentacular differentiation. This is the mechanistic counterpart of what pathologists grade: well-differentiated tumours show lobular architecture and neuronal morphology with Homer-Wright pseudorosettes and a fibrillary matrix, while poorly differentiated tumours lack neural morphology.

nodes.description: Chemotherapy is part of multimodal treatment for locally advanced disease: as induction before local treatment, concurrently with postoperative radiotherapy in patients at high risk of local recurrence, and in the palliative setting. Platinum plus etoposide is described as the most used regimen. Its place is unsettled. The cited review states that although multimodal therapy is agreed to be needed, the optimal use of chemotherapy is still unknown, and reports that the platinum and etoposide combination gave no survival benefit over other regimens. The underlying studies are retrospective.

nodes.description: The genomic landscape is one of large-scale copy number change rather than point mutation. Panel sequencing of 560 tumour-associated genes in a 66-tumour cohort found no highly recurrent mutations, the only recurrently mutated genes being TP53 and DNMT3A, while copy number analysis of the core group showed a high frequency of combined loss of chromosomes 1 to 4, 8 to 10 and 12. A systematic review of the genomics reached the same conclusion, that recurrent mutations are uncommon.
